A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–G provide sufficient readable and matchable evidence for comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original diffusion-model experiments on PDE and particle-dynamics datasets, including quantitative evaluations, ablations, and generated samples in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds penalty-weight sensitivity, augmentation ablations, and a five-spring predictive-model comparison.

M1.justification: The diffusion objectives, constraint-handling procedures, auxiliary prediction heads, backbones, and sampling methods are retained. Data augmentation was already part of v1; v2 adds tests and documentation of it rather than introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate advection, Darcy flow, Burgers, shallow water, three-body, and five-spring dynamics with the same generation and prediction coverage. The added analyses use these existing datasets; the one-step comparison changes evaluation protocol rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds the NRI decoder from Kipf et al. (2018) as an evaluated predictive comparator on five-spring dynamics in Table 11. Existing diffusion, direct-PINN-penalty, FNO, U-Net, and PINN comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: The new five-spring comparison in Table 11 evaluates one-step dynamics error, while its caption identifies the other tables' metric as an eight-step average. New experiments introduce a logarithmic penalty-weight sweep and augmentation-on/off controls. These are limited extensions of the evaluation design.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained matching-objective and Jensen-gap ablations, v2 adds direct permutation-augmentation ablations on both particle datasets, an equivariance-error comparison, and penalty-weight sensitivity testing (Appendices E.3 and E.6, Figure 8, Tables 12–13). These substantially expand scrutiny of distributional-prior enforcement and penalty tuning.

E5.justification: v1 provides point estimates without run-count or seed reporting. v2 introduces uncertainty values in Tables 1–3 and selected rows of Tables 8–9, reporting 3–5 runs with training and sampling seeds varied, except Darcy flow, which varies sampling seeds only. Table 8 discloses five selected seeds and exclusion of seed 2 from all methods after poor noise-matching performance. The meaning of the ± statistic is unspecified.

E6.justification: Numerical results change throughout the principal evaluations and selected appendix rows. For example, Table 3's prior-model three-body trajectory error changes from 1.6072 to 1.9880±0.3418 under the new repeated-run reporting. v2 also adds NRI, sensitivity, and augmentation results. Table 2's advection and Burgers values change by roughly a factor of ten without a corresponding scale explanation, so these updates cannot all be interpreted as comparable performance changes.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, theorem assumptions, constraint derivations, and proofs in Appendices B–F retain their substance. Changes to x versus x_t and explicit time arguments are notational. Adding Mathieu et al. to the attribution of Theorem 11 does not change its statement.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: integrating distributional and physical-feasibility priors into diffusion models to improve physical dynamics generation. The shortened conclusion preserves these claims and their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix E.4 newly discusses difficulty capturing high-frequency details and accumulating errors during longer forecasts. Appendices E.3 and E.6 add interpretations concerning penalty-weight stability and augmentation's support for equivariant noise prediction. These extend the discussion without replacing the original interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 specifies that permutation augmentation jointly permutes particles and connectivity, clarifies Table 4's average trajectory/velocity metric, and discloses the existing eight-step dynamics evaluation. Table 8 also corrects a listed hidden size from 245 to 256. These improve documentation without establishing changes to the underlying implementation.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for GRU, EGNN, PDE-Refiner, geometric neural diffusion processes, and SwinGNN. They support architecture attribution, forecasting limitations, related invariance theory, and the augmentation discussion. The overall related-work organization and novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: Changes include local grammar and notation edits, a condensed conclusion, updated author/publication information, acknowledgments, and additional Appendix E subsections. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the sensitivity plot in Figure 8 and Tables 11–13, revises some captions and table formatting, and replaces the Darcy-flow visualizations and color scales in v1 Figure 10/v2 Figure 11. Existing DPM-solver plots are relocated and renumbered. The overall visual organization remains similar.

improvement.justification: The direct augmentation tests, penalty sensitivity analysis, NRI comparison, and forecasting limitations make v2's empirical argument more informative. Uncertainty and seed-selection disclosures also improve transparency. The gains are limited by excluding a poorly performing seed, leaving the ± statistic undefined, and introducing unexplained numerical or scale discrepancies, including Table 2 and Tables 3 versus 9. The added evidence supports a modest overall improvement.
